quote.after:
For the absolutely continuous curve conclusion (c), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the cited causal-curve calculus and fundamental theorem. The other clauses use the given smooth observer structure, pointwise adapted-chart existence and finite compactness arguments, without these additional curve-calculus premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), and put $n=N/\sqrt{-g(N,N)}$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. In a chart $(U,x)$ put $v^a=dx^a(v)$, $v_s=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v|_{\mathrm e}=(\sum_{a=0}^3(v^a)^2)^{1/2}$.

**(a) Adapted orthonormal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there are a chart $(U,x)$, $x(p)=0$, a radius $r>0$ with $U=x^{-1}(B_r)$, and $K\ge1$, such that on all of $U$
$$n=\partial_{x^0},\qquad g_{00}\equiv-1,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}.$$

**(b) Cone domination.** The chart and radius in (a) can be chosen so every nonzero future causal vector at any point of $U$ satisfies
$$|v_s|\le K v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le K v^0\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad v^0\ge K^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$

**(c) Curve form.** Every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] has strictly increasing time coordinate, and for all $s<t$ in $I$
$$x^0(\gamma(s))<x^0(\gamma(t)),\qquad |x_s(\gamma(t))-x_s(\gamma(s))|\le K\left(x^0(\gamma(t))-x^0(\gamma(s))\right).$$
Consequently every spatial component satisfies the same bound, and the curve image is the graph of a $K$-Lipschitz function into Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ over the interval $x^0(\gamma(I))$.

**(d) Flat minorant cone.** The same chart can be chosen so the constant-coordinate metric $\eta_{16}=-(dx^0)^2+16\sum_i(dx^i)^2$ has every nonzero $\eta_{16}$-causal vector $g$-timelike throughout $U$. If $q,q'\in U$ and $\eta_{16}(x(q')-x(q),x(q')-x(q))<0$, then $q\ll q'$ if $x^0(q')>x^0(q)$, and $q'\ll q$ otherwise.

**(e) General temporal charts: exact compact uniformity.** For any chart $(U',z)$ define its temporal locus
$$P=\{q\in U':\nabla z^0(q)\text{ is past timelike}\}.$$
For every compact set $K_0\subset P$ there is $L\ge1$ such that all nonzero future causal vectors based in $K_0$, with coordinate components and Euclidean norm taken in $z$, satisfy
$$|v_s|\le L v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le L v^0,\qquad v^0\ge L^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$
In particular these bounds hold throughout any relatively compact $U_0\Subset U'$ whose closure is contained in $P$, equivalently whose time gradient is past timelike on its entire closure. Timelikeness merely on $U_0$ gives local bounds at each point and uniform bounds on each compact subset of $U_0$; it does not alone give a uniform bound on all of $U_0$.

No additional choice is used to select the pointwise linear bases or compact cone constants. Countable and Dependent Choice are explicitly required only for the general absolutely continuous curve clause (c), through its actual calculus suppliers.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

after.claim: (Clause (b).) Let $x:I\to M$ be geodesically connectible, $t_1<t_2$ in $I$, and $W$ an open neighborhood of the compact image $x([t_1,t_2])$. Every point of $x([t_1,t_2])$ lies in a strictly convex normal ball contained in $W$ by [L1], and the image is compact, so finitely many such balls $C_1,\dots,C_m\subseteq W$ cover $x([t_1,t_2])$. The preimages $x^{-1}(C_j)$ form an open cover of the compact interval $[t_1,t_2]$; let $\rho>0$ be a Lebesgue number of this cover for the metric of $\mathbb R$. Choose a partition $t_1=s_0<s_1<\dots<s_N=t_2$ of mesh less than $\rho$; then each $x([s_{j-1},s_j])$ lies in some $C_{j}$, and by the defining property of $x$ there is a future causal geodesic in $C_{j}$ joining $x(s_{j-1})$ to $x(s_j)$. Concatenating these finitely many geodesic segments gives a piecewise smooth curve $\eta:[t_1,t_2]\to W$ with the required endpoints; by [L3] it is a locally absolutely continuous future causal curve. This proves (b).

(Clause (a).) Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future causal curve and let $C$ be a strictly convex normal ball with $\gamma([t_1,t_2])\subseteq C$; put $p:=\gamma(t_1)$. The restricted curve $s\mapsto\gamma(t_1+s)$, $s\in[0,t_2-t_1]$, is a future causal curve with image in $C$ starting at $p$, so by [L2] its endpoint $\gamma(t_2)$ lies in $J^+_C(p)$; by [L1] there is $v\in\mathcal C^+\subseteq W_p$ with $\exp_p(v)=\gamma(t_2)$, and the radial geodesic $s\mapsto\exp_p(sv)$, $s\in[0,1]$, is a future causal geodesic whose image is contained in $C$ because $W_p$ is star-shaped and $\exp_p(W_p)=C$. This proves (a).

(Setup for clause (d).) Let $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ be the given future-inextendible curve. Call $T\ge0$ **admissible** when there is a future causal curve $\gamma_T:[-T,\infty)\to M$ with $\gamma_T|_{[0,\infty)}=\gamma$; $T=0$ is admissible. If $T$ is admissible and $q:=\gamma_T(-T)$, then choosing the vector $w_q:=n_q$ (unit future timelike by [L5]) and letting $\rho(u):=\exp_{q}(uw_q)$ be the maximal geodesic, the set $J:=\{u\in\mathbb R:\rho(u)\ \text{is defined}\}$ is an open interval containing $0$ by [L6].

(Clause (c).) If $p\le q$ then either $p=q$ or there is a locally absolutely continuous future causal curve from $p$ to $q$, which is geodesically connectible by step 1.2; conversely, if a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve joins $p\ne q$, apply step 1.1 with $W=M$ to obtain a future causal locally absolutely continuous curve from $p$ to $q$, so $p\le q$ by [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (c). This proves (c).

(Extension step.) With the notation of step 1.3, fix a number $\delta>0$ such that $[-\delta,0]\subseteq J$. For $u\in[-\delta,0]$ the velocity $\rho'(u)$ is the parallel transport of $w_q$, hence is $g$-unit future timelike, so $h(\rho'(u),\rho'(u))\ge1$ by [L5] and $\ell_h(\rho|_{[-\delta,0]})=\int_{-\delta}^0\sqrt{h(\rho'(u),\rho'(u))}\,du\ge\delta$. Define $\gamma':[-\delta-T,\infty)\to M$ by $\gamma'(t):=\rho(t+T)$ for $t\in[-\delta-T,-T]$ and $\gamma'(t):=\gamma_T(t)$ for $t\ge-T$; then $\gamma'$ is a future causal curve: it is continuous at $-T$, the two pieces are locally absolutely continuous, on the first piece the velocity is future timelike everywhere and on the second it is future causal almost everywhere, and the junction is a single parameter value. Hence $T+\delta$ is admissible whenever the maximal geodesic reaches parameter $-\delta$.

(The greedy construction.) Starting from the admissible value $0$ and the curve $\gamma_0:=\gamma$, apply step 2.2 repeatedly: if at stage $n$ the current curve $\gamma_n$ is defined on $[-T_n,\infty)$ and its maximal geodesic extension in the sense of step 2.2 reaches parameter $-\delta$, replace it by the extension $\gamma_{n+1}$ defined on $[-T_n-\delta,\infty)$; if it does not reach $-\delta$, extend instead along its maximal domain $[u_n,0]$ with $u_n>-\delta$ and stop the construction. This produces either a sequence of admissible values $T_n\ge n\delta$ with curves $\gamma_n$ agreeing on overlaps, or a finite chain ending in a curve defined on $[u_n-T_n,\infty)$ whose past parametrization continues the maximal geodesic $\rho$ of the last step up to but not including its past endpoint.

(The union is a future causal curve.) In the first case of step 3.1, the curves $\gamma_n$ agree on the intersections $[-T_m,\infty)$ for $m\le n$, so they define a single map $\gamma^*:\mathbb R\to M$ extending $\gamma$; every compact subinterval of $\mathbb R$ lies in $[-T_N,\infty)$ for some $N$, on which $\gamma_N$ is a future causal curve, so $\gamma^*$ is a future causal curve, because locally absolutely continuous functions agreeing on overlaps glue and the union of finitely many full-measure sets is of full measure ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b)). In the second case the same gluing gives a future causal curve $\gamma^*$ on the half-line $[u_n-T_n,\infty)$ extending $\gamma$.

(Past-inextendibility in the finite-depth case.) In the second case of step 3.1 the curve $\gamma^*$ is defined on $[u_n-T_n,\infty)$ with $u_n>-\delta$, and the last extension piece is the maximal geodesic $\rho$ of step 1.3 with $q$ some point of $M$ and initial velocity the unit future timelike $n_q$: by [L6] and [L7] its image does not have compact closure in $M$, since otherwise the maximal geodesic would be extendible. Consequently $\gamma^*(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t$ decreases to the past endpoint of its domain, so $\gamma^*$ is past-inextendible.

(Past-inextendibility in the infinite-length case.) Suppose the construction gave $\gamma^*$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$, so that by step 3.1 its $h$-length in the past of $0$ is at least $n\delta$ for every $n$, hence infinite. If $\gamma^*(t)$ converged to a point $x\in M$ as $t\to-\infty$, then by [L4], applied in a chart around $x$, the $h$-length of the tail $(-\infty,t_0]$ would be finite, a contradiction. Hence $\gamma^*$ does not converge at $-\infty$, so it is past-inextendible.

(Clause (d) concluded.) In both cases the constructed curve extends $\gamma$ on $[0,\infty)$ and is past-inextendible by step 4.2 and step 5.1; it is future-inextendible because it agrees with the future-inextendible curve $\gamma$ on $[0,\infty)$, so convergence at $+\infty$ of the extension would be convergence of $\gamma$. This proves (d), and the past version follows by reversing the parametrization.
